history.summary: Shree Maa Kali Mandir stands on Kali Sthan Road at New Daily Market, Lower Bazaar, in the heart of Ranchi, Jharkhand, dedicated to Goddess Kali. It is described as one of Ranchi's oldest temples: one source calls it more than 200 years old but gives 1919 as the build year, while another says the stone idol was installed around 1850 — the founding date is CONFLICT (verify). An akhand lamp is said to have burned in the temple for about a century, and morning aarti begins around 7 AM. Coordinates are approximate for the Lower Bazaar area — exact temple coordinates are not published (verify).

name: Shree Maa Kali Mandir, Ranchi
town_description: Ranchi is the capital of Jharkhand, set on the Chota Nagpur Plateau at about 650 metres above sea level. Known as the 'City of Waterfalls' for the many falls around it, it blends tribal heritage, colonial-era landmarks and modern industry. It is the main pilgrimage base for the temples and festivals of the plateau region.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi — about 7-8 km (verify)
travel.road: New Daily Market, Lower Bazaar, in central Ranchi; reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw or taxi
